subtitle.en: Building a giant, decaying freighter out of simple modules — and learning to let plain surfaces stay plain.
subtitle.zh: 用简单的模块搭出一艘巨大的、正在朽坏的货轮——并学会让朴素的表面就那样朴素着。

blocks.en: The shipwreck is an area of the island that has not been shown before, because up until recently it was one of the barest, most undeveloped areas we had. It grew bigger and bigger over the years (like most things on the island), from a little slab mockup Jon had by the shore, into a massive freighter with the usual,  intricate gameplay requirements.
blocks.zh: 沉船是岛上一直没对外展示过的一个区域，因为直到不久前，它还是我们手上最空、最没开发的区域之一。这些年来它越变越大（就像岛上大多数东西那样）：从 Jon 在岸边摆的一小块板状草模，长成了一艘巨大的货轮，还带着那些一如既往、繁复琐碎的玩法要求。

blocks.en: The process for building this ship was interesting. We have architects helping us with building designs, but even the architects were not entirely familiar with the structures of ships. We spent a lot of time looking at reference images, talking about the materials and how the entire structure would decay over time. They gave me a base design for the hull, deck, bridge, and the inner beams of the ship. I modeled that whole, then split it up into five pieces.
blocks.zh: 造这艘船的过程挺有意思。我们有建筑师帮忙做建筑设计，但就连这些建筑师也谈不上熟悉船体结构。我们花了很多时间看参考图，讨论该用什么材料、整艘船的结构会如何随时间朽坏。他们给了我船壳、甲板、舰桥和船内横梁的基础设计。我照着把整艘船建了模，然后把它拆成五块。

blocks.en: The front, middle, and back pieces were kept somewhat intact, the rest was split into scattered rubble to dress the scene. Next, it was time to figure out the gameplay and decide what parts of the ship would be accessible and what parts would be rotten away. Because the ship was so huge and I was modeling it alone, I had to be careful about limiting what would be navigable and what would be seen, since I wanted to keep my workload to a minimum while still having very interesting, believable areas. I spent a long time cutting holes, bending floors and ripping out beams.
blocks.zh: 前、中、后三块基本上保持完整，其余的都被拆成散落的瓦砾，用来点缀场景。接下来就该琢磨玩法了：决定船上的哪些部分可以到达、哪些部分已经朽烂掉。因为船实在太大，而我是一个人建模，所以我必须谨慎地限制哪些地方可以走通、哪些地方会被看到——我想把自己的工作量压到最低，同时又要让区域足够有趣、足够可信。我花了很长时间在船体上开洞、把地板掰弯、把横梁扯下来。

blocks.en: Then, I had to figure out how to make a decaying heap of metal with our simple, clean style, as described by Eric in the last post. My first attempts had minimal detail in the geometry, with a lot of noise and contrast in the textures. It was exactly the opposite of what we usually do, but I was trying to develop a process for detailing the entire ship quickly, and it's a lot faster to use blendmaps to add noise than to tediously cut and shape geometry. It looked terrible, but I was at a loss for how to make it better quickly. Fortunately, Luis and Eric encouraged me to just reduce the contrast in the textures, and let the small details in the modeling stand on their own. It took ten seconds to lighten some textures, and all of a sudden I had something I was finally happy with. At first it felt wrong to leave large surfaces so plain, but the other artists were right. With our beautiful lightmaps and simple style, a little detail and a few modular rubble and rust pieces were all that was needed to make the space feel like it belonged to our game.
blocks.zh: 接着，我得想办法用 Eric 在上篇里描述的那种简洁干净风格，做出一堆正在朽坏的金属。我最初的尝试是：几何体上几乎没有细节，贴图里却塞满噪点和高对比。这跟我们平常的做法正好相反，但当时我在试着摸索一套快速给整艘船加细节的流程，而用混合贴图（blendmap）加噪点，比费劲地去切割和塑形几何体快得多。结果看起来糟透了，而我又想不出怎么快速改好。幸运的是，Luis 和 Eric 鼓励我把贴图的对比度降下来，让建模里那些小细节自己站住。把一些贴图提亮只花了十秒，突然之间我就得到了一个自己终于满意的结果。起初我觉得把这么大的表面留得这么素是不对的，但另外两位美术说得对。有我们漂亮的烘焙光照贴图和简洁的风格，只需要一点点细节，再加几块模块化的瓦砾和锈迹，就足以让这个空间感觉像是属于我们这个游戏的。

blocks.en: This shipwreck is still not quite finished, but it is the last huge project on my plate before moving on to the many smaller projects and tasks we still need to complete to ship the game.
blocks.zh: 这艘沉船还没完全做完，但它是我手头最后一个大项目；接下来就要转向那许多小项目和小任务了——为了把游戏做出来，我们还得把它们都完成。
